title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 119–121): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial framework ("figures", "subdivisions", "supports", "ateliers", "magasins", "ensembles adonnés") for a kind of tame or stratified geometry. This continues the 'topologie modérée' programme sketched in Esquisse §5–6. Σ = Σ_A is the ordered set or category of supports (subsets) attached to an atelier A.

The problem he has found (p.119) is an internal contradiction. So far he has only handled constructible supports and operations on them. Yet the presentation X|Y already forces him to consider strata X, Y that need not be constructible, or even 'commensurable'. At the same time, he wants an intrinsic description of the supports underlying a figure, as objects of Σ, independent of the figure or subdivision chosen.

This page:
- (1) He wonders whether his instinct deceived him 'for once'. He resolves to be very careful whenever he invokes support considerations.
- (2) He states the goal: relate the supports attached to a figure to those attached to a subdivision of it. The relation should not be affected by two subdivisions being non-'commensurable', i.e. lacking a common refinement or join. He asks whether this vague requirement can be made precise.
- (3) Alternative: work only with the subcategory Σ_cons ⊂ Σ_A of constructible supports. On it the operation ∁ (complement) is everywhere defined, while Sup and Inf are only partially defined.
- (4) He asks for a construction of this independent of the 'preadditive' structure of Σ (continued on p.121). Page 121 proposes obtaining the constructible sets of a magasin-atelier F by 'inverting' the subdivision arrows (localization of (F, ≪) at refinement maps). He is unsure whether the result is an 'ensemble adonné' embedding into Σ. He notes that in the Boolean case (pre-Boolean or 'faithful' ateliers) there is no problem.

In modern terms, the question is how to define the Boolean algebra of definable or constructible sets of a tame space intrinsically: as a colimit or localization over the system of triangulations/subdivisions, rather than via an ambient algebra of subsets. The obstruction is that two subdivisions may have no common refinement, which is the classical Hauptvermutung-type issue.
errors: No mathematical claims are asserted, only questions, so there is nothing to refute.

Minor tension: in a Boolean algebra of constructible sets, finite Sup/Inf would normally be total. Their being only 'partially defined' presumably reflects his specific Σ_A (supports relative to subdivisions), not ordinary constructible sets. This is not explained on the page.

ideas.what: Requirement that supports of a figure be intrinsic, independent of the chosen subdivision, even when two subdivisions have no common refinement ('commensurability')
ideas.modern_name: Invariance under subdivision / common refinement problem (Hauptvermutung-type issue); definable sets of an o-minimal structure as intrinsic objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (Steinitz, Tietze, Milnor's counterexample 1961); o-minimal triangulation (van den Dries, Shiota)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures in general terms, not this specific formalism

ideas.what: Restricting to the subcategory Σ_cons of constructible supports, with complement total and Sup/Inf partial
ideas.modern_name: Boolean algebra (or partial lattice) of constructible/definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chevalley (constructible sets), EGA IV (Grothendieck), model theory (definable sets)
ideas.where_published: Constructible sets in EGA IV §1.8–1.9; this atelier version unpublished

ideas.what: Seeking a construction of constructible sets independent of the 'preadditive' structure; next page proposes localizing the category of subdivisions at refinement arrows
ideas.modern_name: Localization / colimit over refinements (cf. PL spaces as colimits over triangulations; Grothendieck ring of definable sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL topology folklore; Krajíček–Scanlon and Denef–Loeser for Grothendieck rings of definable sets

missed.claim: An open question: define supports intrinsically for a combinatorial 'atelier' formalism of tame geometry so that they are insensitive to non-commensurable subdivisions. A candidate (continued p.121) is to recover constructible sets by inverting refinement maps, without using the preadditive structure of Σ. Grothendieck leaves it unresolved except in the Boolean case.
missed.quote: une relation qui ne soit pas affectée par le fait que les deux subdivisions ne soient pas "commensurables" ... peut-il se préciser ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete axiomatic question about combinatorial foundations of tame topology, a counterpart to o-minimality via subdivisions. It is mildly interesting for historians of Grothendieck's 'géométrie modérée' work, but it overlaps heavily with known o-minimal triangulation theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is self-critical, exploratory foundational musing within the unpublished atelier formalism. It contains no finished results. The underlying issues (subdivision invariance, constructible Boolean algebras, localization at refinements) are well known in other guises.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'm'[devr- crossed out]aurait-il trompé, pour une fois ?', probably continuing 'Mon instinct ...' from p.119.
'Je voudrais [...] donc aux supports' is more likely 'J'en viendrais [/J'en viens] donc aux supports attachés à une figure'.
'une [...] "quel ne soit[?] affecté' is probably 'une relation qui ne soit [pas] affectée par le fait que'.
'ne soient "commensurables" — ou "joint"[?] une' is probably 'ne soient [pas] "commensurables" — ce "joint"/"flou" ... peut-il se préciser ?' (uncertain).

'formée des supports[?] constructibles, avec des dispositions 𝒞' is likely 'formée des parties constructibles, avec des opérations ∁ (partout définies) et Sup et Inf (partiellement définies seulement)'. Here ∁ is the complement symbol.
Last lines are probably 'Peut-on expliciter une construction indépendante de la condition / notion préadditive de Σ' (continued on p.121).
